q1_issues.issue: (Ongoing sk_tend_1) asserts at top level that a tending is underway, but the sentence says only that the Council permits the apprentice to begin one; the complement of a control verb is to assert nothing about occurrence.

q2_gaps: a permission-granting matrix VERB ("the Council permits an apprentice to V"): whether it is only an ordinary object-control event, or additionally licenses a deontic record on the complement, or (as a standing policy over an indefinite) the kind-level reified permission property, is not addressed — the deontic sections key on a modal or a passive/participial deontic, never on a permitting verb with its own agent

the inception pattern's mandatory (Ongoing <activity>) when the begin event is itself an unasserted complement: the inception rule and the control-verb "no tense/status, occurrence not stated" rule pull opposite ways and neither is subordinated to the other
a capitalized definite common-noun institution ("the Council"): whether it counts as a proper noun requiring a Name atom or as an ordinary definite description is not settled
notes: Object control is handled correctly — the begin event reified at top level, attached to the matrix verb by Theme, with the object controller copied in as its Agent and no tense of its own — and the simple present rightly gets no status atom on the permitting. "Solo" recorded as a Manner filler in its surface form is licensed, and the indefinite "an apprentice" correctly takes a witness under a verbal predicate.
